attackOnCentralClaim:
The central claim has two halves and they do not survive equally.

HALF ONE — "a type system that refuses to compile an unsourced claim" — SURVIVES, with the marketing trimmed. Making `evidence` non-optional on `Claim` and `statusSource`/`ledeSource` non-optional on `Project` genuinely converts M1 from a review discipline into `tsc --noEmit`, which is already an M4 gate command, so the instrument costs nothing new. What the gate actually proves is ATTACHMENT, not relevance: `{kind:'repo', url:'https://github.com/Swately/PhyriadFG'}` satisfies tsc and the `new URL()` protocol test for literally any sentence about PhyriadFG. The candidate is honest that it cannot verify resolution, less honest that it cannot verify aptness. It survives because M1 as frozen measures exactly attachment — "enumerate every such rendered assertion, count those with attached evidence" — so the claim is true against the metric it is scored on. But it holds by the metric's letter, not by the epistemics the thesis advertises.

HALF TWO — "makes two real figures resolve on GitHub Pages" — SURVIVES and is the strongest verified thing in the candidate. I opened climx's EstadoCard.tsx: `estadoImg(ides) => ${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}img/estados/${ides}.webp` is real, and generalizing it is a mechanism port, not a resemblance. I opened the portfolio's vite.config.ts: `base: '/portfolio/'` is real and already there. Under the objective's fixed host referent this is a genuine production-only failure class, and AT0 fix 3 was written to make exactly this countable.

THE IMPLICIT COMPETITOR — is it a strawman? Partly. The thesis is framed as a bet that clicking to a source beats navigating ("a reader who can click any sentence to its source in one hop trusts the page more than a reader who can navigate it"). Nothing in the objective makes those alternatives. A four-route design can carry the identical Claim/Evidence type, the identical footnote grammar and the identical assetUrl helper, and additionally collect the router, its test suite, NotFound and PrimitivesLab. So the sacrifice is real but the dilemma is manufactured: the candidate is trading M6 headroom for a reading-comfort preference and calling it a principle. To its credit it says so plainly in weakestPoint and refuses to farm P2 — which the objective explicitly forbids farming anyway.

WHERE IT WINS: the objective's named workload almost exactly. A recruiter arriving cold, scrolling once, wanting to check whether "runs on silicon" is a boast — one hop from the sentence to PHarvard's §State, no route change, no back button, no lost scroll position, and the two figures are already on screen as zero-click evidence. That reader is served better here than by any design that puts proof one navigation away.

WHERE IT EMBARRASSES ITSELF: the scanner. Three of five projects carry no figure — I confirmed no screenshot of climx live, Phynned's UI or PHarvard's board exists on disk — so after two figures the page is an unbroken column of Spanish prose punctuated by mono footnote brackets, and the design cannot fix that later because 175 KB of M3(b) headroom absorbs one more screenshot of trazado_1's class, not three. Secondly, and recorded rather than scored because O2 forbids scoring it: for O1's largely non-Spanish audience, dense footnoted prose is the format that degrades worst — a tile design still surfaces language-independent proper nouns, versions and URLs to a reader who cannot read the sentences; an essay does not.

smugglingCheck:
No smuggling found, and the refusals are unusually explicit and checkable.

STATE PHOTOGRAPHS (FORBIDDEN): not present in any form. The design ports the MECHANISM the objective explicitly blessed — the BASE_URL helper, the onError degrade, loading="lazy" — and points it at the operator's own diagrams. It goes further than required and declines EstadoCard.module.css outright (inventory entry #8, rated medium), on the reasoning that the equal-height flex column, the overflow:hidden radius and the hover-moves-accent rule all exist to serve a card grid this design does not have. I read that CSS file: all three rules are exactly what it says they are, and all three have no consumer in a one-column prose layout. Declining it is the correct call and it is the single clearest anti-smuggling signal in the candidate.

DROPPED DRIVERS: the data layer, geo layer, SearchCombobox and every weather-specific component are absent. Where the design touches a donor that carries dropped code — CreditsPage — it strips useFetch, useMunicipioIndex, ErrorState, groupByState and all 1,474 rows and keeps only the native <details>/<summary> shell, which I confirmed is the pattern the inventory rates that file for. It then declines to COUNT even that toward M6.

THE ROUTER: not smuggled back under another name. The three in-page anchors (#proyectos, #herramientas, #sobre-esta-pagina) are plain fragment links, not a route matcher; there is no <Link>, no popstate handling, no fallback page. And the public/404.html port is materially REDUCED, not disguised: I read climx's original and confirmed the design drops the ?/<path> encoding, the ~and~ escaping and the main.tsx restore block, keeping only origin + '/portfolio/' + hash. That is a smaller thing honestly labelled smaller, not a router wearing a shim's clothes.

ONE THING WORTH NAMING, NOT A SMUGGLE: MEASUREMENTS.md is counted as an M6 unit for content transcription. That is not a forbidden or dropped driver — it is pool entry #11, high-value, legitimately in scope — but counting a doc as 'structural work' stretches the metric rather than reintroducing anything banned. Filed under F2, not here.
optimalityHonesty:
No unscoped absolute optimal/best claim found. Every superlative in the candidate is bounded to its own port list or to the page: "the strongest of the four" (of its four new ports), "the most literally structural resource on the page", "the second-weakest of my four new ports", "the port an adversary is most entitled to strike". Those are internal rankings, not claims about the design space.

The thesis sentence is a bet, not a verdict — "betting that a reader who can click any sentence to its source in one hop trusts the page more" — and the weakestPoint section actively argues against the candidate's own survival, which is the opposite failure mode from optimality inflation.

Two phrases I checked because they assert about the frozen objective rather than about the design, and both are true: "which is exactly the class of host-dependent bug the objective's M6 fix 3 was written to make countable" matches AAP_OBJECTIVE.md lines 90-93 verbatim in substance, and "the objective states M6 is a floor and not a maximand... P2 cannot be farmed" matches lines 108-110.

The one place honesty runs the wrong way is not inflation but deflation: presenting "reading (iii) -> 2 -> trips K2" as a live failure mode when the frozen M6 wording does not support the restriction that reading invents. Recorded as a defect, but it is the opposite of an optimality claim.

defects.finding: M6 headline of 7 does not survive an independent deletion test; my recount is 5 (6 at most). MEASUREMENTS.md is struck: what lands in the portfolio is transcribed prose inside content.ts, and deleting it removes information, which is neither 'breaks the page' nor 'removes a capability' — the metric's two disjuncts. tokens.css is contested: delete it and every var() falls to invalid, but the page still renders and every sentence is still readable, which is the closest thing in this list to the 'merely a style' the metric excludes. This matters materially because the A3 tie-break ranks by M6 count at position (iii): a headline of 7 against a true 5 distorts the ranking input even though the target of >=4 is still met on my own count.

M1 is claimed at 100% but the tools <dl> breaks it. The design closes that section 'by construction' by having each of the 6 rows name the project that evidences it — but naming a project elsewhere on the same page is a cross-reference, not one of M1's four accepted evidence types (repo URL, live URL, project diagram, or a number traceable to that project's own docs). Each row asserting that a project uses a tool is a rendered capability assertion about a project, i.e. an M1 unit. Worst case 22/28 = 79% against a target of 100%. Bounded and trivially closable by linking the row's project name, but the design never says it does, and M1 sits under P1.

Contrast arithmetic error on the accent token. The candidate reports --color-accent #2255cc on #ffffff = 6.5:1. I recomputed with sRGB linearization and D65 coefficients: R 34/255 -> 0.01600, G 85/255 -> 0.10327, B 204/255 -> 0.60305; L = 0.2126(0.01600) + 0.7152(0.10327) + 0.0722(0.60305) = 0.12080; contrast = 1.05/0.17080 = 6.15:1. Reported figure is 5.7% high. Both clear AA and the accent is neither body nor muted text, so M5(c) is unaffected — but the candidate presents these four numbers as computed rather than estimated, and one of the four is wrong.

Miscalibration in the pessimistic direction: 'reading (iii) — newly-ported executable code only — gives TWO, which trips K2 and disqualifies the design outright.' The frozen M6 says 'Count of DISTINCT climx resources doing structural work in the portfolio'. It contains no 'newly ported by this candidate' qualifier and no 'executable code only' qualifier; both are the candidate's inventions. Its real K2 margin on my recount is 2-3, not zero. Filed as a defect because a self-report that understates its own compliance distorts the convergence step in the same way an overstatement does.

The thesis oversells what the type gate proves. 'A type system that refuses to compile an unsourced claim' is accurate; the surrounding framing ('the reader goes claim -> proof in one click') implies the gate underwrites proof. It does not: a required discriminated-union field is satisfied by any well-formed https URL, so a repo-root link attached to a specific numeric claim compiles clean and passes the new URL() protocol test. Survives against M1 as frozen, which counts attachment; does not survive as an epistemic guarantee.

index.html is unaccounted for. It is absent from newFiles and from all five milestones, yet it currently carries lang="en", an English <title> and an English <meta name="description"> — I read it. Under a design whose whole premise is one dense Spanish page, the document element declares English to assistive technology and to search engines. No frozen metric catches it (jsx-a11y lints JSX, not index.html; M5(b) names landmarks, not lang), and it costs zero bytes — but the design enumerates thirteen page sections exhaustively and never reaches the head, while the very donor file it ports (climx's 404.html) sets lang="es".

The M6 evidence for assetUrl is stronger than its test. assetUrl.test.ts is specified to assert 'the BASE_URL prefix', but under vitest import.meta.env.BASE_URL resolves to '/', not '/portfolio/'. The test can therefore prove string concatenation and reject a leading slash, but cannot detect the base misconfiguration that is the port's entire justification — that check only exists in the M-D manual step (preview at /portfolio/ with the network panel). Related: the new 80% coverage gate on src/lib/** is justified as 'the data/logic layer appearing' while the layer is one two-line function, so the gate is near-vacuous as written.

salvageables: Making evidence a non-optional field on the Claim type so that `tsc --noEmit` — already an M4 gate command — becomes the first M1 instrument: an unsourced sentence about a project is a compile error rather than a review oversight. Costs no new tooling and no bytes.

content.test.ts freezing each project's status as a literal transcribed from that project's README, so README drift breaks CI. This converts M2 from a manual page-vs-README diff into an automated gate, which is worth having in any design regardless of page structure.

Generalizing climx's estadoImg() into assetUrl(path) => `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}${path}` pointed at the operator's own images — the mechanism the objective explicitly blessed while forbidding the state photographs it originally served.
Escalating climx's onError degrade from hiding the to hiding the WHOLE

Rendering Phyriager's own README caveat — port to 26.2 in progress, mod builds but is not validated live, a git clone yields no working bot today — as a first-class claim beside the version string. Verified against the README; it is strictly stricter than the 5/5 M2 asks for.

Refusing to print climx's live Lighthouse numbers because MEASUREMENTS.md records them against https://swately.github.io/project-tw/, before the repository was renamed. Printing no number instead of a stale one is the discipline the page is trying to demonstrate, applied to itself.

Adopting MEASUREMENTS.md's governing rule — 'Every estimate is replaced here by a real number, with date + instrument. No entry, no claim.' — as the colophon's rule, so the page's own figures cannot be written with placeholders before M-D and M-E produce them.

Executing the per-resource M6 deletion test for real — remove the file or block, run `npm run build && npm run preview` at /portfolio/, record whether the page fails to render, loses a capability, or merely changes appearance — instead of arguing the count in prose. This is the M6 instrument the objective implies but no candidate is obliged to actually run.

The explicit anti-padding ledger: naming CreditsPage's <details> pattern as used-but-not-counted, folding app.tsx's shell into the reset.css entry rather than counting the same skip-link capability twice, and declining climx's README and ARCHITECTURE.md as two further content units on the grounds that they are one capability arriving through three files. Whoever wins should carry this discipline into their own count.

Naming, in each tools <dl> row, the project that evidences the tool — so no capability is asserted about the operator without a project above it that backs it. The mechanism does not close M1 as the candidate claims, but the intent is right and one added link would close it.

Wrapping each in-column figure in an <a> to the full-resolution PNG, because the ~44rem editorial measure renders the multi-GPU diagram's box labels too small to read — and restating the diagram's content in Spanish prose in the <figcaption>, since I confirmed every label in phyriadfg_multigpu.png is English.

attackOnCentralClaim:
The thesis is that a type system refusing to compile an unsourced claim, plus a print-footnote grammar, buys more trust than navigation does. Half of it survives first-hand checking and half of it does not.

WHAT SURVIVES. The compile-time gate is not rhetoric. `npm run typecheck` is already an M4 command (package.json, read first-hand), TypeScript is strict (tsconfig), and a non-optional `evidence` field on a discriminated union does exactly what is claimed: a new sentence about a project without a source is a build failure. Of the mechanisms available for M1, this is the only one that moves the metric out of reviewer judgment and into CI. Its evidence targets are real: I confirmed `sw/hwcheck.s`, `syn/VENDOR_VS_ESTIMATE.md` and `DIAGNOSIS.md` exist in PHarvard, and I confirmed all five projects carry a git `origin` at github.com/Swately/<name> (PhyriadFG additionally carries a `chlmateus` fork remote, which is not what the page links to). The footnote grammar is honest about its own reach: figures are wrapped so a load failure hides caption and image together, because an orphan Spanish caption asserting an unseen image is a false statement.

WHERE IT EMBARRASSES ITSELF. First, the gate covers `Project`, and the page's opening lede is not a Project. That lede asserts five project capabilities in one sentence and is the first thing the 20-second reader meets — so the assertions least covered by the thesis's machinery sit at exactly the reader position the named workload fixes. Second, 'unsourced' and 'unverifiable' are not the same predicate. The test asserts `new URL()` parses with protocol https; a link to a renamed file, a wrong heading slug, or a repo that was never pushed compiles, passes, renders, and reads as proof. The candidate declares this in contentGaps, which is honest, but the thesis is stated as though the gate settles credibility and it settles only well-formedness. Third, the candidate applies MEASUREMENTS.md's discipline unevenly: it correctly refuses the live Lighthouse rows because they were measured against the pre-rename project-tw URL, then lifts '~350 B gzip per municipio file (2026-07-28)' without noticing that the same document's 2026-07-31 table supersedes it — 'forecast 3/1 = 344 B gz → 463 B gz'. A page whose whole argument is traceability prints a number its own cited source retired.

IS THE COMPETITOR REAL? Inside the thesis, yes — 'a reader who can navigate it' is a live sibling angle, not a strawman. But the honest-competitor question is the one that hurts. For the named workload — an engineer or recruiter outside Mexico, arriving from a GitHub profile, twenty seconds — a well-written English GitHub profile README beats this page on two axes and I will say so. (a) It is zero hops from where that reader already is, and every proof link on this page points back into GitHub anyway, so the page is a detour to reach the thing it cites. (b) Language: the reader is largely non-Spanish-speaking, and a single dense Spanish page is precisely the artifact that cannot be skimmed by a non-speaker — a multi-route design at least offers headings and a route name as skim surface. That second point is O2's recorded tension, frozen and explicitly not scored, so it changes no number here; but it is a real finding about D3 specifically, because the angle's own bet is 'maximum reading', and reading is the operation this reader cannot perform.

WHERE IT WINS. The skeptical Spanish-reading engineer who wants to know whether 'runs on silicon' is a boast. This page hands them hwcheck.s and VENDOR_VS_ESTIMATE.md inline beside the sentence, and puts '0.1.0-experimental' plus 'the mod builds but has not been validated live' in the heading next to Phyriager's name. No README card grid does that, and P1 is the objective's top priority.

WHERE CONSUMABILITY BREAKS. Five <details> 'Cómo verificarlo' blocks holding `python syn/build_vendor.py`, `testbench.ps1`, `npm run coverage`. Nobody screening a candidate runs a Lattice vendor toolchain. Those blocks are typed as Claim[] and therefore feed M1's numerator — they serve the metric more than the reader, which is completeness mistaken for communication. And the nav offers #proyectos / #herramientas / #sobre-esta-pagina but no per-project anchor, so a phone reader who came for PHarvard scrolls past four notes to reach it. The h3-carries-name-plus-status line is a genuine skim layer and stops this from being fatal, but it is the only one.
